transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-12-05 14:30 PST
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Lydia (Fjordlane Head ML), Tom (VP Eng), Sanjay (FinOps), Asha (Security)

Summary (auto):
Maya opened with a QBR-style snapshot: usage trending up 23% month-over-month, spikes during routing batch jobs, cost creep on generation tokens. Team discussed tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated), a short pilot for dedicated reserved capacity during holiday peak, and a plan for a stress test + follow-up cost workbook. Security clarified SOC2/HSM expectations and data residency. Next steps: cost sheet, stress tests, compliance artifacts.

Topics:
- Usage trends and forecast
- Cost drivers and per-route economics
- Reliability incidents and tail-latency mitigation
- Pilot scope: dedicated capacity for holiday window
- Security/compliance ask list

Action items (brief): see metadata action_items above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, uh we've got about 45 minutes today, quick winter readiness readout — usage, costs, reliability, and then a short roadmap sync. Eva— Evan will run through the technical spots.
[00:22] Evan: yeah hi, hi all, I'll kick off with the perf slides that I shared — note, the KV cache hit rate on the beam routes dropped from 82% to about 67% during the November surge. That increased token regen which pushed cost.
[00:40] Lydia: got it, that matches what we saw in the app logs — more cold starts for sessioned chat flows. We also changed prompt templating which may be a factor.
[00:55] Tom: can you say that again, cold starts? Are we talking latency spikes or cost spikes?
[01:05] Evan: both, so the KV cache misses cause the runtime to re-evaluate attention states, which increases tail latency — spikes to 1.8s from a 300ms baseline on some queries — and of course more tokens generated = higher spend.
[01:25] Sanjay: quick question: how much of the cost bump is from model choice vs repeated generation? do we have per-model per-route breakdown?
[01:34] Maya: yes we do, I pulled a high level but Evan will share a more granular sheet. Roughly 60% of the incremental spend was from the 'conversational-rewrite' route hitting a larger model during surges. The rest was regen from cache misses and retries.
[01:58] Lydia: that route is critical for our user retention flow though, so we can't just downsize without quality checks.
[02:08] Evan: agreed. We have a couple options: 1) switch that route to a quantized variant and tune prompts, 2) enable prefix/KV caching more aggressively, 3) reserve dedicated capacity to keep warm and avoid cold chains during bursts.
[02:27] Tom: dedicated sounds appealing for holiday peaks but it's also a contractual commitment, right?
[02:33] Maya: correct, dedicated is reserved — monthly commit — but you get predictable throughput and lower per-token at scale plus isolation. We can do short-term burst reservations too, or a hybrid where critical routes run on Dedicated and everything else on Hosted.
[02:55] Sanjay: what's the delta in unit cost for dedicated? ballpark numbers?
[03:00] Maya: ballpark — dependent on QPS and model, but we've seen 20-45% unit cost reduction on heavy sustained workloads when using Dedicated with the right config (batching + quantization). I'll include a model-specific table.
[03:15] Asha: from security perspective, if we go Dedicated we still need to confirm VPC, SSO/SAML integration, and whether the customer-managed KMS/HSM is required. Our compliance team will want audit logging and retention guarantees.
[03:31] Evan: we support VPC peering for Private/Dedicated and can integrate with customer KMS for key management, and we surface audit logs — I'll attach the audit log sample.
[03:42] Asha: great, can you also confirm whether the logs include token-level redaction? we need PII gating.
[03:49] Evan: there's configurable redaction; in our hosted default we avoid raw prompt storage unless you opt in. For Dedicated/Private we can set retention windows and pipeline redaction.
[03:59] Lydia: circling back to reliability — what error modes did we see in November?
[04:05] Evan: two main incidents: 1) a long tail latency event correlated with autoscaler thrash when regions received uneven load, and 2) a transient OOM on a quantized model variant under sustained long-context requests. We patched autoscaler thresholds and adjusted kernel memory allocation; the OOM fix required switching to an alternative kernel and limiting effective seq length.
[04:30] Tom: autoscaler thrash — is that something we can replicate in a lab? we want to see behavior under holiday microbursts.
[04:37] Evan: yes — we can run burst-load tests simulating traffic patterns you provided; goal would be to reproduce scaling transitions, KV cache warmup behavior, and measure tail latency. We recommend a 3x peak simulation for the holiday window.
[04:50] Lydia: can you include jitter in that simulation? our real traffic is chatty and has lots of short tails.
[04:55] Evan: yep, we'll shape the traffic with poisson jitter and some long-tail sessions.
[05:02] Sanjay: financially, I'm concerned about commit vs on-demand spend. If we do a one-month dedicated window, what's the upfront and refund policy?
[05:12] Maya: our Dedicated contracts have minimum commit terms but we can do a reserved holiday window pilot with a limited-term addendum; I'll work with sales to structure a short reserved pilot — finance usually wants a firm spend floor but we can negotiate.
[05:25] Tom: okay timeline-wise — we need a decision by Dec 15 to have capacity reserved for the late-December peak. That's our internal procurement cutoff.
[05:34] Maya: noted. so action items: we'll send a per-route cost breakdown with model/quantization recs, Evan will run burst stress tests, and Asha will give the compliance list.
[05:45] Asha: quick security nit — we require SOC 2 Type II and periodic pentest results for any vendor hosting production data; do you have an up-to-date pack?
[05:54] Maya: yes we have SOC 2 and penetration test summary; I'll drop the security pack link in slack and across the sheet.
[06:00] Lydia: one more on quality — if we move to a quantized model variant, what is the expected delta in response quality for the rewrite route? any eval numbers?
[06:08] Evan: short answer: varies by model. For our Llama-derivative quantized 8-bit path we saw ~2-4% drop on BLEU-style metrics on paraphrase sets, but for human evaluation the difference was often negligible for short prompts. We'll attach a small eval run targeted at your rewrite prompts.
[06:25] Tom: can someone share the eval harness and the prompt set you used? we'd like to review.
[06:29] Evan: yes, I'll share the harness repo link and run a tailored eval with your prompt set — we can run side-by-side: baseline vs quantized variant.
[06:36] Sanjay: regarding billing visibility — can we get token-level line items per route in our invoice export? We need visibility to allocate back to product squads.
[06:44] Maya: we can provide token-level exports per route and per model. We also have route tagging so you can map spend to squads. I'll include an example CSV in the cost workbook.
[06:54] Lydia: what's the expected time to implement KV cache tuning? is it config-only or does it need code change on our side?
[07:02] Evan: mostly config — changes to TTLs and prefixing strategy; we might suggest a small prompt shim to normalize prefixes for better hit rates, that's a small dev task on your side but low lift.
[07:15] Tom: good. Regarding rollouts, we'd want canarying + automatic fallback — if we deploy quantized route we want a safety valve to go back to baseline model if quality drops.
[07:24] Evan: Redwood supports route rollouts with canary percentages and automatic rollback based on configured quality thresholds or error rates; we'll propose a rollout policy in the follow-up.
[07:34] Maya: roadmap note — in Q1 we're rolling out improved batching heuristics and a new kernel selection optimizer that should further reduce unit cost for long context workloads. That could be relevant for your long-session users.
[07:47] Lydia: great — any ETA on the kernel optimizer?
[07:50] Maya: early Q1 beta, general availability mid-Q1. We'll see whether it makes sense to include the pilot in that beta.
[07:58] Tom: last logistics question — is there a day/time window you prefer for the stress test? we need it not to collide with our internal deploys.
[08:06] Evan: we're flexible next week and week after — propose Wed 12/15 morning PST for a full run, then a shorter follow-up on 12/17 for analysis.
[08:16] Tom: sounds good, we'll block 12/15 in the calendar tentatively.
[08:20] Maya: quick recap before close — we'll deliver: cost workbook + per-route table, stress test and logs, security pack + compliance list, and an eval run for quantized vs baseline. Decision deadline from your side: 12/15 for holiday reserved capacity. Anything else?
[08:36] Sanjay: please include sample contract language for a short reserved window so our procurement team can pre-review.
[08:41] Maya: will do.
[08:43] Lydia: thanks everyone, this was useful.
[08:45] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.
